title: MCP C# SDK 2.0 Makes HTTP Stateless by Default and Adds Multi Round-Trip Requests
gist: Microsoft released stable MCP C# SDK 2.0 implementing the 2026-07-28 Model Context Protocol revision, which the SDK team calls the largest since launch: HTTP is stateless by default, routing headers are standardised, and Multi Round-Trip Requests replace server-initiated mid-call input.

insights.claim: MCP C# SDK 2.0 removes the initialize handshake and the Mcp-Session-Id header; protocol version and capabilities now travel with every request, so any server instance can handle any request without sticky routing or shared session stores.
insights.speaker: Edin Kapić
insights.so_what: Stateless MCP makes agent tool servers far easier to scale horizontally behind standard load balancers.
insights.quote: The initialize handshake and the Mcp-Session-Id header are gone.
insights.locator: The initialize handshake and the Mcp-Session-Id header

insights.claim: The SDK team describes the 2026-07-28 specification revision as the largest since the protocol launched because it rethinks how MCP works over HTTP, and HttpServerTransportOptions.Stateless now defaults to true.
insights.speaker: Edin Kapić
insights.so_what: Default flips shape how most new MCP servers are deployed, shifting the ecosystem toward cloud-native patterns.
insights.locator: MCP is an open protocol that standardises

insights.claim: tools/call requests now carry Mcp-Method and Mcp-Name headers and an [McpHeader] attribute can promote a tool parameter to an Mcp-Param-* header, letting load balancers and gateways route on headers without reading the body; the body stays authoritative and a mismatch returns HeaderMismatch.
insights.speaker: Edin Kapić
insights.so_what: Gateway-level routing and policy for MCP traffic becomes feasible, opening room for infrastructure vendors.

insights.claim: Statelessness removes the channel servers used to ask clients for input mid-call, so MRTR replaces it: a tool throws InputRequiredException with input requests plus an opaque requestState, and the client re-issues the call with inputResponses.
insights.speaker: Edin Kapić
insights.so_what: Interactive human-in-the-loop tools must be redesigned as request/response retries rather than persistent sessions.

insights.claim: Roots, sampling and logging APIs are deprecated under MCP9005 following SEP-2577, and Tasks moved to an opt-in ModelContextProtocol.Extensions.Tasks package incompatible with the experimental version in 1.3 and 1.4.
insights.speaker: Edin Kapić
insights.so_what: Early adopters of experimental MCP features face migration cost and breaking changes.

insights.claim: One reader asked whether the protocol guards requestState against tampering or reuse across sessions, and no reply appeared in the comments.
insights.speaker: Edin Kapić
insights.so_what: Pushing state to the client creates an unaddressed integrity question that security teams will need to answer.
insights.quote: One reader of the announcement asked whether the protocol guards requestState against tampering or reuse across sessions; no reply appeared in the comments.

insights.claim: The release enforces stricter OAuth behaviour (RFC 9207 issuer validation, mandatory advertised PKCE S256 support, inferred application type in dynamic client registration), and the team says its next focus is end-to-end authentication and authorisation.
insights.speaker: Edin Kapić
insights.so_what: Auth is the acknowledged gap for enterprise MCP adoption.
insights.locator: According to the announcement, stable 1.x APIs keep working

insights.claim: Version 2.3 made McpClient.ServerInfo nullable, a source-breaking change, and the notes warn against using self-reported server identity for security decisions.
insights.speaker: Edin Kapić
insights.so_what: Server identity in MCP is untrusted metadata, so client-side trust models must not rely on it.

insights.claim: Modern Streamable HTTP responses now wait for the first protocol message before sending headers, so silent long-running handlers may need progress output or a longer HTTP timeout.
insights.speaker: Edin Kapić
insights.so_what: Upgrades can silently break slow tools through timeouts, a migration risk for production agents.
insights.locator: Modern Streamable HTTP responses now wait
